note: Every party is a simulated identity on one machine under one operator. B3 is this file's own 40-line rule over the replay's records, modelled on requester-accepted debit notes; it is not Golem's implementation. Keys are fresh on each run; the amounts are deterministic.

rows.note: the operator doubles the count in the top acknowledgment; its signature fails

rows.goal: G2 shift credit between stages (one stage colludes)
rows.note: stage1 signs the requester's terms with weights 1 and 99
the operator withholds stage0's acceptance; stage0 presents its own records
no record names a reservation its requester did not sign

rows.goal: G5 charge an attempt a stage abandoned
rows.note: stage0 vanished after 2 acknowledged outputs; the signed terms say nobody pays. B3 charges the accepted prefix by design.

rows.case: P1 requester stops acknowledging after 10 of 40 outputs

replay.reason: the requester stopped acknowledging; the outputs it acknowledged are charged

rows.note: the stages stop at the signed allowance in both schemes, so the unpaid outputs are the same

rows.case: P1b requester withholds the last acknowledgment of a finished 40-output answer

replay.reason: the answer was completed; the outputs the requester acknowledged in time are charged

rows.case: P6 the final stage drops after 10 of 40 outputs and never closes

replay.reason: the release window passed without every stage closing; under these terms nobody is charged or paid

rows.note: the replay's provider-loss-free rule: an abandoned answer is free. B3 has no such rule.

rows.case: P7 the stages end the answer themselves after 10 of 40 outputs and close as failed

replay.reason: a stage ended the answer before it finished; under these terms nobody is charged or paid

rows.case: L3 the same final stage signs K + 1 steps it never sent, then closes

replay.reason: the requester stopped acknowledging; the outputs it acknowledged are charged

rows.note: the provider-loss-free rule is defeated by the final stage alone: the gap reads as the requester withholding, so the abandoned answer is charged. Both schemes now charge the prefix.

rows.case: L1 stage0 withholds its closing receipt after the whole answer was delivered and acknowledged

replay.reason: the answer was delivered and acknowledged, but no in-time closing receipt was presented for stage 0

rows.note: one stage vetoes every stage's payment, and the requester keeps a free answer. Under B3 the accepted counts are owed without any closing receipt.

rows.case: L2 the requester acknowledges all 40 outputs, then signs a second acknowledgment of count 40 with another chain
rows.note: the requester's own contradiction voids its charge. It can sign it afterwards: signers write their own signedAt. B3 takes the highest accepted count.

rows.case: L4 a stranger signs its own terms, acceptance and charge binding under this reservation ID

replay.reason: terms signed by more than one requester name this route; nothing is inferred

rows.note: three signatures from a key that took no part make the real reservation undecidable. B3 keys an agreement by reservation and requester, so the stranger's agreement is a separate one that charges only the stranger.
